observationTitle: Quarterly privileged-access recertification was not evidenced
observationDescription: The review of 18 privileged accounts identified 4 accounts with no retained quarterly recertification approval and 2 accounts whose business owner had changed without an access review.
riskSummary: Privileged access may remain active after the underlying business need changes, increasing the risk of unauthorised system activity.
rootCause: Access recertification is coordinated by email and the completion evidence is not retained in a single accountable record.
criteria: ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A — identity and access management controls; IIA Standards — sufficient, reliable and relevant evidence.
recommendation: Introduce a quarterly owner-certified privileged-access review with named evidence, exceptions and closure tracking.
managementResponse: Management agrees. The control owner will implement the recommendation and provide completion evidence for Internal Audit verification.

observationTitle: Bank reconciliation review evidence was incomplete
observationDescription: Three of twelve monthly bank reconciliations sampled showed preparer evidence but no dated reviewer sign-off before the following month-end.
riskSummary: Errors or unusual reconciling items may remain undetected and carry into subsequent reporting periods.
rootCause: The checklist requires preparation but does not enforce reviewer completion before the close is marked complete.
criteria: IIA Standards — control effectiveness should be supported by sufficient evidence; approved finance close procedures.
recommendation: Make reviewer sign-off a mandatory close control and escalate reconciliations that remain unreviewed after five working days.
managementResponse: Management accepts the observation and has assigned an owner to complete the corrective action within the agreed date.

observationTitle: Loan override approvals were retained outside the credit file
observationDescription: For 5 of 25 sampled facilities with pricing or policy overrides, the approval existed in email but was not linked to the final credit decision record.
riskSummary: The cooperative may be unable to demonstrate that exceptions were authorised within delegated limits.
rootCause: Override approvals are not a required attachment before the credit workflow can be completed.
criteria: Approved credit policy; IIA Standards — traceability of evidence supporting control conclusions.
recommendation: Require the final approver record and rationale to be attached before an override can move to disbursement.
managementResponse: Management accepts the observation and has assigned an owner to complete the corrective action within the agreed date.

observationTitle: Dormant member account monitoring was not consistently documented
observationDescription: The monthly dormant-account report was generated, but evidence of investigation was absent for 7 of 30 sampled reactivated accounts.
riskSummary: Unusual reactivations may not receive timely challenge, increasing fraud and member-protection risk.
rootCause: The control relies on branch follow-up without a standard review record or closure field.
criteria: Internal member-account monitoring procedure; risk-based monitoring expectations.
recommendation: Record reviewer disposition, evidence and closure for each flagged dormant-account reactivation.
managementResponse: Management accepts the observation and has assigned an owner to complete the corrective action within the agreed date.

observationTitle: Emergency changes were not retrospectively reviewed within target
observationDescription: Four of eleven emergency production changes sampled were reviewed more than ten working days after implementation.
riskSummary: Control failures introduced by emergency changes may persist without timely independent challenge.
rootCause: The change calendar records implementation but does not trigger overdue retrospective-review reminders.
criteria: ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A — change management; approved change procedure requiring timely retrospective review.
recommendation: Create an automated reminder and escalation at three and five working days after an emergency change.
managementResponse: Management accepts the observation and has assigned an owner to complete the corrective action within the agreed date.

observationTitle: Supplier master amendments lacked independent verification
observationDescription: Six supplier bank-account amendments were supported by request forms, but two lacked evidence of an independent callback before payment details changed.
riskSummary: Fraudulent bank-detail changes could redirect supplier payments before detection.
rootCause: The verification step is described in procedure but is not a required system field.
criteria: Approved supplier master-data procedure; segregation-of-duties control principles.
recommendation: Require a recorded independent verification reference before bank-detail changes become effective.
managementResponse: Management agrees. The control owner will implement the recommendation and provide completion evidence for Internal Audit verification.

observationTitle: Branch cash surprise counts were below the planned frequency
observationDescription: The Nakuru Branch completed seven surprise cash counts against a plan of twelve during the review period.
riskSummary: Cash shortages or control breaches may remain undetected for longer than intended.
rootCause: Count ownership is not reassigned when the branch operations lead is unavailable.
criteria: Approved branch operations control schedule.
recommendation: Assign a backup count owner and track completion against the monthly control schedule.
managementResponse: Management accepts the observation and has assigned an owner to complete the corrective action within the agreed date.

observationTitle: Backup restore testing did not cover the member portal
observationDescription: The annual restore exercise demonstrated database recovery for the core platform but did not include the public member portal configuration and deployment package.
riskSummary: A recovery event may restore data but leave the member-facing service unavailable.
rootCause: The recovery test scope is based on database assets and does not use a complete service dependency inventory.
criteria: ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A — information backup and ICT readiness for business continuity.
recommendation: Extend the recovery test scope to application configuration, dependencies and end-to-end service validation.
managementResponse: Management accepts the observation and has assigned an owner to complete the corrective action within the agreed date.

observationTitle: Competitive quotation exceptions were not centrally tracked
observationDescription: Four procurements above the internal quotation threshold used exception approvals, but there is no consolidated register showing rationale, approver and cumulative value.
riskSummary: Repeated exceptions may bypass competitive sourcing without management visibility.
rootCause: Exception approvals are retained in individual procurement files without portfolio-level monitoring.
criteria: Approved procurement policy and delegated authority limits.
recommendation: Maintain a quarterly exception register and report repeat suppliers, values and approval rationale to management.
managementResponse: Management accepts the observation and has assigned an owner to complete the corrective action within the agreed date.

observationTitle: Leaver access closure was not reconciled to HR exit dates
observationDescription: Two of fourteen sampled leavers retained at least one application account for more than two working days after the recorded exit date.
riskSummary: Former staff may retain access to cooperative systems after employment ends.
rootCause: HR exit notifications are sent by email and completion is not reconciled against application-owner confirmations.
criteria: ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A — identity lifecycle controls; approved exit checklist.
recommendation: Use a single leaver checklist with application-owner completion evidence and ageing escalation.
managementResponse: Management accepts the observation and has assigned an owner to complete the corrective action within the agreed date.
